1.caption: Figure 1. The ARBITER assessment workflow. A language-model agent searches and reads captured trial documents, records answers and selects evidence. Software binds selected text to the captured extraction, applies the RoB 2 algorithms to propose ratings, and exports the assessment record. A reviewer may approve a proposed result in the general workflow. In the benchmark, the harness supplied the assigned target and the interactive approval step was not tested. The reviewer receives an HTML report and an audit file. In the audit-file box, 'source' refers to source identifiers and selected evidence; complete source files are not included. Binding identifies a location in the captured text; it does not establish that the passage supports the answer.
1.alt: A language-model agent searches captured trial documents, records answers and selects evidence. Software binds selected text to the captured extraction, applies RoB 2 algorithms and exports an assessment record. Reviewer approval belongs to the general workflow and was not tested in the benchmark. The audit file contains source identifiers and selected evidence, not complete source files. Binding locates text and does not establish that it supports an answer.
1.title: The ARBITER assessment workflow

2.caption: Figure 2. Each answer is tied to stored sources, and RoB 2 rules compute the rating across every domain. AVATAR compares early surgery with watchful waiting in asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis; the outcome is all-cause death. This trial was chosen to illustrate the process, not as representative. Rows link paraphrased questions, source excerpts, AI answers, software checks and domain ratings. Letter/page tabs identify sources; “Weighed against” and “Open point” give counter-evidence and unknowns. In this example, a No information answer about the dated analysis plan contributes to the overall judgment of Some concerns. Full answers and official question wording appear in the linked repository AVATAR answer and evidence records. Y, yes; PY, probably yes; PN, probably no; N, no; NI, no information. The footer compares the Published D5 label with the subsequent blinded D5 choices from both human reviews; it does not report independently rated Overall judgments. The example reproduces a model assessment; the displayed rationales were not independently validated. The illustrated P value is compatible with chance but does not itself establish that randomization was adequate. [23] The overall rule shown is simplified: multiple domains with Some concerns can justify an overall High judgment when they substantially lower confidence in the result. The illustrated trial has one Some concerns domain. [1]
2.alt: AVATAR's five domains link source excerpts, model answers, software checks and ratings. Four domains are Low. A No information answer about the dated analysis plan contributes to Some concerns for selection of the reported result and Overall. Counterevidence and unknowns remain visible. The figure illustrates a model assessment; its rationales were not independently validated. The simplified Overall rule does not show every permitted escalation.
2.title: Each answer is tied to stored sources, and RoB 2 rules compute the rating across every domain

3.caption: Figure 3. Parallel assessment lanes and conditional blinded-label choices. ARBITER, Direct prompting and Human Reviewers assess the same benchmark. Both AI arms assessed the same 102 trials using the same reported model identifier and supplied documents. Two human reviewers independently recorded ratings and signalling answers for all 510 trial-domain cells before viewing labels. In a separate stage, each chose among three labels presented in random order without rationales. The conditional choice estimate uses 60 agreed choices from 80 arm-cells where the two arms disagreed; 20 split choices enter sensitivities. The all-cell human reviewer comparisons are not restricted to that conditional population. Counts are trials or cells as indicated; no interval applies.
3.alt: Three parallel assessment lanes for ARBITER, Direct prompting and two independent human reviews across 102 trials and 510 domain cells. A separate conditional branch contains 80 arm-discordant cells, 60 agreed choices and 20 splits.
3.title: Parallel assessment lanes and conditional blinded-label choices

4.caption: Figure 4. Absolute and paired domain agreement with each independent human reviewer. Blue circles denote ARBITER and orange squares Direct prompting. Left panels show exact agreement with 95% intervals on a 0–100% scale; right panels show paired ARBITER minus Direct prompting differences in percentage points, with neutral diamonds and zero lines. Each human reviewer contributes 510 pooled cells and 102 per domain. Agreement between the human reviews is 388/510 (76.1%; weighted κ 0.59), context rather than a performance ceiling. The compact Published comparison retains all 510 cells. D1: randomisation process; D2: deviations from intended interventions; D3: missing outcome data; D4: outcome measurement; D5: selection of the reported result.  CI, 95% confidence interval; 10,000 percentile bootstrap replicates, trials resampled within meta-analysis; seed 20261018.
4.alt: Exact agreement and paired gains against each human reviewer, pooled and by domain. Both pooled gains favor ARBITER; D5 gains are largest and D3 depends strongly on the human reviewer reference. The full-cohort Published comparison is shown separately.
4.title: Absolute and paired domain agreement with each independent human reviewer

5.caption: Figure 5. Paired signalling-answer diagnostics. Rows cover all five domains against each human reviewer; n is the number of question components evaluable in both arms. Diamonds and bars show ARBITER minus Direct prompting exact agreement and 95% intervals. Five-level matching distinguishes yes, probably yes, no, probably no and no information. Collapsed matching combines yes/probably yes and no/probably no, leaving no information separate. These are different estimands. D1: randomisation process; D2: deviations from intended interventions; D3: missing outcome data; D4: outcome measurement; D5: selection of the reported result. D3 and D5 illustrate reference dependence and the effect of coding. eTables 11–13 contain source-specific domain summaries, complete paired question contrasts and eligibility accounting for both codings. CI, 95% confidence interval; 10,000 percentile bootstrap replicates, trials resampled within meta-analysis; seed 20261018.
5.alt: Paired signalling-answer differences by domain and human reviewer, separating five-level and collapsed coding. D3 changes direction with coding against Human Review 1; D5 collapsed gains are smaller against Human Review 2.
5.title: Paired signalling-answer diagnostics

notes: Rating categories are Low, Some concerns and High; each source contributes 510 domain cells.
